text:
One concept that has helped me significantly on higher timeframe trades is using light, "pilot" positions.

A pilot position lets me get a feel for the rhythm of a market before committing size. 

It gives me exposure, feedback, and emotional alignment without forcing full conviction too early.

I'm sure many traders wait for “confirmation” before entering, usually a reclaim, a breakdown, deviation, or some clean level-to-level trigger. I used to think the same way... But from experience the problem is that by the time confirmation is obvious, I'm giving up asymmetry... 

For me, confirmation is not always the reason to start a position, more often, it is the reason to add.

The pilot is the probe. 

Confirmation is my permission to size with dynamic risk.

I think the short around 81.5 was readable from a price action pov, there was enough structure/rejection to build a case for it, but personally I'd have felt as though I'm just guessing, not playing an actual probability vs the conviction, timing and confidence I get from profile and flow - (my own performance over the last few years tells me that)..

That said, I mainly use orderflow for futures/perps, where the venue level auction tends to be cleaner and more actionable. 

With equities etc.., I only use volume and market profile, not so much orderflow as in footprints etc because my approach is more momentum based, and equity flow is fragmented across venues, dark pools, various data feeds..

Personally volume profile and orderflow don’t replace price action, they add context/confluence around it.

Price action gives me the setup -  profile/orderflow helps refine execution, invalidation, and conviction.

If I were starting again, I’d learn pure price action and volume first. Structure, liquidity, acceptance/rejection, failed auctions, range behaviour, trend days, etc. 

Only after that orderflow. Otherwise it’s easy to get lost in the approach without understanding what price is actually doing.

Just to add that a trade setup isnt a strategy, but a strategy contains a given trade setup and many other facets of a trade, risk, position sizing etc - how you structure the trade... excuse the typos - grammar
